title: Logistics Warehouse Office Rates: Calculating Front Office & Dispatch Square-Foot Cleaning Proposals
seoTitle: Logistics Warehouse Office Rates: Dispatch Cleaning Cost per Sq Ft
metaDescription: Logistics warehouse office rates: $1.15-$2.39 per sq ft monthly for dispatch suites with driver restrooms. Model your bid in our cleaning cost calculator.
excerpt: A warehouse front office and dispatch suite costs more per square foot to clean than a comparable downtown office because drivers, dock grit, and shared restrooms compress the workload into a small footprint. This guide shows the per-visit and monthly math, restroom density adders, and the frequency most distribution centers settle on.
quickAnswer: Using national benchmarks, a 1,800 to 3,200 sq ft warehouse dispatch office typically runs about $240 to $590 per visit and $2,075 to $7,660 per month, or roughly $1.15 to $2.39 per sq ft per month, depending on restroom count and whether you clean two or three nights a week. Larger cross-dock admin areas of 10,000+ sq ft fall closer to $1.00 to $1.74 per sq ft per month because the base rate drops to $0.07 to $0.12 per sq ft per visit.

blocks.text: Why dispatch offices price differently from standard office suites

A warehouse front office looks small on a floor plan, usually 1,500 to 6,500 sq ft tacked onto a 150,000 sq ft distribution building. The problem for a cleaning vendor is that this small footprint absorbs traffic from three populations at once: salaried office staff, hourly warehouse associates who cut through on breaks, and outside truck drivers who check in at the dispatch window and use the nearest restroom. A downtown office of the same size might see 25 occupants a day. A busy dispatch office can see 25 occupants plus 60 to 150 driver visits per shift, every one of them tracking dock grit, rain, and road salt across the threshold.

That is why vendors rarely quote these spaces off a simple production-rate sheet. The base per-square-foot rate is only the starting point. What moves the bid is restroom density, the floor finish between the dock door and the dispatch counter, and the number of nights you need the space reset. If you understand how each of those levers is priced, you can read a proposal line by line instead of comparing bottom-line numbers that were built on different assumptions.
Benchmark rates by warehouse office size and frequency

The scenarios below use our national pricing model: a size-bracket rate per sq ft per visit, multiplied by a flooring factor (1.04 for VCT, 1.05 for mixed carpet and hard floor) and a frequency factor (1.0 at twice weekly, 0.95 at three times weekly), plus $15 to $30 per restroom per visit and optional add-ons. Monthly totals use 8.66 visits for twice weekly and 13.0 visits for three times weekly, which is the 4.33 weeks-per-month convention most janitorial contracts follow.

blocks.caption: Warehouse front office and dispatch cleaning cost scenarios (national average, before local labor adjustment)

blocks.text: Notice that the 1,800 sq ft shack and the 3,200 sq ft front office land in a similar per-square-foot band even though one has a single restroom. Small spaces sit in the under-2,500 sq ft bracket at $0.12 to $0.20 per sq ft per visit, and the vendor still has to drive a crew to the site, sign in at the guard shack, and stage equipment. The 3PL office drops to $0.90 to $1.52 per sq ft per month because it crosses into the 2,500 to 9,999 sq ft bracket and only needs two nights a week. Every visit is also subject to a $90 to $135 minimum, which is why tiny dispatch trailers rarely price below about $780 a month even at two nights a week.

blocks.title: Labor-hour cross-check
blocks.text: ISSA-style production for open office space averages about 3,500 sq ft per labor hour. For the 3,200 sq ft, three-restroom front office, our model expects roughly 1.25 to 1.9 labor hours per visit once restroom minutes are added. If a bid assumes 45 minutes for that space, expect missed restrooms; if it assumes four hours, ask what else is in the scope.
Restroom density: the line item drivers create

Restrooms are where dispatch offices diverge most from standard offices. A typical 3,200 sq ft professional suite has two restrooms serving 20 people. A dispatch office of the same size often has three or four: a men's and women's set for office staff, a single-occupant driver restroom accessible from the check-in vestibule, and sometimes a locker-adjacent restroom shared with the warehouse floor. At $15 to $30 per restroom per visit, each additional fixture room adds $195 to $390 a month at three visits a week.

items: Driver restrooms take the hardest use: high urinal and floor-splash load, paper towel overuse, and after-hours access when gates stay open for late appointments. Price them at the top of the $15 to $30 band.

Enzymatic urinal screens with a 30-day service life, such as the Fresh Products Wave 3D screens, cut odor complaints between visits and let you hold a two- or three-night schedule without a midday restroom check.

Controlled one-at-a-time towel dispensers like the Tork Elevation Matic H1, which holds a 1,000-ft roll behind a key lock, reduce overflowing trash and the number of restock trips a day porter would otherwise make.

If the vendor supplies paper and soap, expect $0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit on top of labor; for 3,200 sq ft at 13 visits that is about $500 to $1,040 a month, heavily driven by driver restroom usage.
Ask whether the warehouse-side locker restroom is in scope. Many bids silently exclude it and then bill it as an extra once the first complaint arrives.

blocks.text: Traffic wear between the dock door and the dispatch counter

Most warehouse front offices are finished in VCT or sealed concrete because carpet does not survive pallet-jack wheels and steel-toe boots. VCT carries a 1.04 flooring factor in our model for neutral-pH damp mopping and periodic buffing, but the real cost is the restoration cycle. Grit from the dock acts like sandpaper on acrylic floor finish, and a dispatch lane that gets 100 driver visits a day can wear through its finish in three to four months rather than the nine to twelve you would see in a corporate lobby.

Budget a quarterly or semi-annual strip-and-recoat program for the traffic lane and a scrub-and-recoat for the rest of the office. Amortized monthly, deep floor care runs about $0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft, so a 3,200 sq ft office should carry $96 to $192 a month for it. Vendors who use a commercial stripper and high-solids acrylic finish system, such as the Zep two-gallon strip-and-polish bundle, typically lay four to five coats in the dispatch lane and three elsewhere. Pair that with a 6 to 10 ft walk-off mat run inside the dock entry and you can stretch the restoration interval by a full cycle.
Recommended weekly frequency for distribution center offices

items.name: Count real occupancy, not headcount
items.text: Add daily driver check-ins to office staff. Under 40 combined daily users, twice weekly with a restroom-only midweek touch usually holds. Over 40, plan three nights minimum.

items.name: Match frequency to shift pattern
items.text: Single-shift DCs can be cleaned after the office closes. Two- and three-shift operations need the crew to work around a live dispatch desk, which slows production and argues for a day porter instead of more night visits.

items.name: Separate restroom frequency from office frequency
items.text: Restrooms in driver-heavy offices often need five-day service while desks and offices need only two or three. Ask vendors to price restroom-only visits against the $90 to $135 minimum.

items.name: Set the floor program on its own calendar
items.text: Write the quarterly strip or scrub dates into the contract rather than leaving them to the night crew's discretion, so you can verify they happened.

blocks.text: For most single-shift distribution centers with a 2,500 to 6,500 sq ft front office, three nights a week is the practical sweet spot. Moving from three nights to five raises visit count from 13.0 to 21.65 per month while the frequency factor only drops from 0.95 to 0.90, so a full five-night program usually costs 55 to 60 percent more for incremental benefit in the offices themselves.
How to read a dispatch office proposal line by line

Ask every bidder to break the price into base square footage, per-restroom charges, consumables, and the amortized floor program. When those four lines are visible, you can see whether a low bid is low because the vendor is efficient or because it excluded the driver restroom and the quarterly floor work. Also confirm who controls gate and alarm access: if the crew has to wait for a supervisor to open the dock-side door, that idle time ends up in the hourly rate, which for standard janitorial labor already runs $35 to $65 per hour.

Plug your front office square footage, restroom count, and floor type into the Office Cleaning Cost Calculator, then load competing bids into the Quote Comparator to see which vendors priced the driver restrooms and floor program honestly.

faqs.q: What is a fair price per square foot to clean a warehouse front office?
faqs.a: On our national model, a dispatch office between 2,500 and 9,999 sq ft prices at $0.09 to $0.15 per sq ft per visit before flooring and frequency factors, plus $15 to $30 per restroom per visit. Monthly that works out to roughly $0.90 to $2.39 per sq ft depending on restroom count and nights per week. Apply your local labor multiplier before comparing bids, since metro areas with high janitorial wages can run 20 to 40 percent above the national figures.

faqs.q: Should the warehouse floor be included in the office cleaning contract?
faqs.a: Usually not. Warehouse floors are maintained with ride-on scrubbers on a separate industrial scope and priced by the hour or by machine pass. Keep the office contract limited to the conditioned office envelope, the dispatch vestibule, driver restrooms, and break areas, and list the boundary on a marked floor plan so nobody argues about who owns the dock threshold.

faqs.q: How do vendors calculate monthly visits for a three-night schedule?
faqs.a: Most US janitorial contracts use 4.33 weeks per month, so three nights a week equals about 13 visits a month and five nights equals 21.65. If a proposal multiplies by 4 weeks it is understating annual cost by about 8 percent, and the gap usually reappears as extra-service invoices in months with five Mondays.

faqs.q: What insurance should I require from a cleaner working in a distribution center office?
faqs.a: Request a certificate of insurance showing at least $1 million per occurrence and $2 million aggregate general liability, statutory workers compensation, commercial auto, and a janitorial or third-party crime bond. Name your company and the building owner as additional insureds, because the crew will walk past high-value freight and dock equipment even if the scope stops at the office door.

faqs.q: Do driver restrooms trigger any OSHA requirements for the cleaning crew?
faqs.a: Restroom cleaning itself does not require a bloodborne pathogens program, but if crew members are expected to clean up blood or bodily fluids, OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030 applies and the vendor should document training, PPE, and hepatitis B vaccination offers. Every chemical on site must also have a current SDS under the HazCom standard, 29 CFR 1910.1200, accessible to both the crew and your staff.
